frontier.hypothesis: Target fills jump_insn 344's slot DESPITE the update_block marker, so the marker is harmless in target for a reason that is not 'no marker' - most likely mark_target_live_regs' target_hash_table cache: the entry for the opposite thread is reused when tinfo->bb_tick == bb_ticks[b], and update_block bumps bb_ticks only for find_basic_block(the moved insn), which need not be the opposite thread's block.
frontier.mechanism: mark_target_live_regs (reorg.c:2520-2560) hashes on INSN_UID(target) and returns the cached live set unchanged when the block tick matches. update_block (reorg.c:2276) bumps bb_ticks[find_basic_block(insn)] only. If in target the moved insn (li v0,0x19) and the opposite thread resolve to different blocks - which depends on where the previous BARRIER sits, i.e. on whether an unconditional jump precedes the `||` test - the poisoned recomputation never happens and the clean cached set is used.
frontier.next_probe: On the BASE body, dump `DBRDBG mtlr target=<uid> block=<n>` lines from tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s19/dbr_base.txt for the opposite thread of jump_insn 344 and note whether mark_target_live_regs recomputed or hit the cache. Then test the BARRIER hypothesis in C: make the block immediately before code_label 347 end in an unconditional jump (e.g. spell the first disjunct of the `||` as `if (cond1) goto sel_block;` with the D_800A38A8 block written between the two tests so it ends with `goto block_49;`), which inserts a BARRIER and moves find_basic_block's resolution for the marker's insn to a different block than the opposite thread's. Score twice and re-read oppregs/setsopp for jump_insn 344.

frontier.hypothesis: The store sink (emitted 83-88, ~2 pts) and the arm store (emitted 148, ~1 pt) are the cheapest remaining cluster and have never been attacked on the 10-floor chassis - s13 closed them byte-exactly with a `goto do_calls` but that same goto cost cluster A on the 17-floor body, which no longer applies since s16 re-attributed cluster A to the duplicated-call pair.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 sinks `sh v0,0x286(s0)` into the first jal delay slot (E-s13-1); target keeps it at the head of the shared store/calls block. s13's variant A reproduced target's slots 83-95 and 144-157 exactly via a source-level `goto do_calls`, and was rejected only because it lost cluster A on a body whose cluster A came from a different mechanism. The s16 body wins cluster A from nrefs(arg1)=9 supplied by the `<` arm's duplicated calls, which variant A's goto does not disturb in the same way.
frontier.next_probe: Re-measure s13's variant A construction on TOP of the current 10-floor body (memory/grind/func_800283D0/rejected/variant-A-arm-goto-docalls-store-and-arm-byte-exact-clusterA-lost-17.c is the 17-floor version; port only its `goto do_calls` store placement onto candidate.c, keeping the s16 `<` arm intact). Score twice, then run tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s18/al.sh to confirm the $s2/$s3 seats survived.

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster B closure and the store-sink closure compose: a body that closes the store sink first may pay the W2b copies more cheaply, because the two `move v0,v1` copies land in different scheduling positions once the store is not sunk into the jal delay slot.
frontier.mechanism: W2b's +2 is two `move v0,v1` copies materialised at emitted 128/131. Both sit in the region the store sink also touches; s17 already measured that the store pin and cluster A interact (tC held both at 12/221). If the store is pinned at the block head, the copies may coalesce or land in slots that already differ from target.
frontier.next_probe: Only after frontier item 2 lands a body materially below 10: re-apply W2b's `s16 sel5` change on top of the store-pinned body and score twice. If the result is below the store-pinned body's own floor, cluster B becomes free and the frontier reopens; if it is +2 again, the copies are independent of the store and the hoist family is finally closed.
